extracted.intended_audience: Applicants, licensees, and spectrum lessees seeking FCC declaratory rulings or guidance on foreign ownership and related compliance (broadcast and common carrier entities)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for petitions for declaratory rulings under the FCC's foreign ownership framework (calculation of indirect interests, insulation criteria, routine terms/conditions, notifications, and continuing compliance). Applies to broadcast and common carrier applicants, licensees, and their subsidiaries/affiliates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification of maximum percentages for advance approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner shall specify for the named foreign individual(s) or entity(ies) the maximum percentages of equity and/or voting interests for which advance approval is sought or, in lieu of a specific amount, shall state that the petitioner requests advance approval for the named foreign individual(s) or entity(ies) to increase their interests up to and including a non-controlling 49.99 percent equity and/or voting interest in the licensee, for petitions filed under § 1.5000(a)(2), or in the controlling U.S. parent of the licensee, for petitions filed under § 1.5000(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording requires petitioners to either specify precise maximum percentages or request approval up to non-controlling 49.99% depending on petition type (§1.5000(a)(1) vs (a)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of petition information per §1.16 and §1.5000(c)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant, licensee, or spectrum lessee filing a petition for declaratory ruling shall certify to the information contained in the petition in accordance with the provisions of § 1.16 and the requirements of § 1.5000(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition filings must include required certifications; see §1.16 for general certification rules and §1.5000(c)(1) for any additional content requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of standard-question responses to the Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: For each petition subject to a referral to the executive branch pursuant to § 1.40001, the petitioner must submit responses to standard questions, prior to or at the same time the petitioner files its petition with the Commission, pursuant to subpart CC of this part, directly to the Committee for the Assessment of Foreign Participation in the United States Telecommunications Services Sector (Committee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standard questions and instructions are available on the FCC website; the required information shall be submitted separately from the petition and directly to the Committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely delivery of complete unredacted petition copy to the Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete and unredacted copy of its FCC petition(s), including the file number(s) and docket number(s), must be submitted to the Committee within three (3) business days of filing it with the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions for submitting the copy to the Committee are available on the FCC website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcast applicants' certifications (point of contact; accuracy; notification; penalties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadcast applicants and licensees shall certify: (i) to designate a point of contact who is located in the United States and is a U.S. citizen or lawful U.S. permanent resident for execution of lawful requests and as agent for legal service of process; (ii) that the petitioner is responsible for the continuing accuracy and completeness of all information submitted and agrees to inform the Commission and the Committee of any substantial and significant changes while a petition is pending and, after the petition is no longer pending, to notify changes promptly and within 30 days; and (iii) that the petitioner understands failure to fulfill conditions or material falsity may subject them to remedies including revocation/termination and criminal and civil penalties, including penalties under 18 U.S.C. 1001.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are mandatory certifications for broadcast applicants; they include both procedural duties (designated U.S. contact, timely notification of changes) and acknowledgement of enforcement consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common carrier applicants' certifications (CALEA, availability of records, point of contact, accuracy, penalties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common carrier applicants, licensees, or spectrum lessees shall certify: (i) to comply with all applicable Communications Assistance for Law Enforcement Act (CALEA) requirements and related rules and FCC orders; (ii) to make communications to, from, or within the United States, as well as records thereof, available in a form and location that permits them to be subject to valid and lawful requests or legal process in accordance with U.S. law (including the Wiretap Act, Stored Communications Act, Pen Register and Trap and Trace Statute, and other court orders/subpoenas); (iii) to designate a U.S.-based point of contact who is a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident; (iv) that the petitioner is responsible for continuing accuracy and completeness and must notify Commission/Committee of substantial changes and changes after the petition within 30 days; and (v) that failure to fulfill conditions or material falsity may lead to remedies including revocation/termination and criminal and civil penalties, including penalties under 18 U.S.C. 1001.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies compliance obligations with U.S. law and law enforcement access requirements in addition to certification and notification duties similar to broadcast applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity interests held indirectly — calculation by successive multiplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Equity interests that are held by an individual or entity indirectly through one or more intervening entities shall be calculated by successive multiplication of the equity percentages for each link in the vertical ownership chain, regardless of whether any particular link in the chain represents a controlling interest in the company positioned in the next lower tier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a foreign individual's 30% in Corp A and Corp A's 40% in Parent B yields 12% (30% × 40% = 12%) in Parent B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting interests through corporations — successive multiplication with >=50% treated as 100%
rubrics_metrics.description: Voting interests held through one or more intervening corporations shall be calculated by successive multiplication of the voting percentages for each link in the vertical ownership chain, except that wherever the voting interest for any link in the chain is equal to or exceeds 50 percent or represents actual control, it shall be treated as if it were a 100 percent interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 30% × (a controlling 70% treated as 100%) = 30% voting interest flows through.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting interests through partnerships — general/uninsulated vs insulated rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Voting interests held through one or more intervening partnerships shall be calculated depending upon whether the individual or entity holds a general partnership interest, an uninsulated partnership interest, or an insulated partnership interest. A general partner and uninsulated partner shall be deemed to hold the same voting interest as the partnership holds in the company situated in the next lower tier of the vertical ownership chain; a partner shall be treated as uninsulated unless the operative agreement satisfies the insulation criteria in § 1.5003. An insulated partner (limited partner satisfying insulation criteria) shall be deemed to hold a voting interest equal to the partner's equity interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: the Commission presumes that a general partner of a general partnership or limited partnership has a controlling interest and is uninsulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting interests through limited liability companies — manager/member insulation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Voting interests held through one or more intervening limited liability companies shall be calculated depending upon whether the individual or entity is a non-member manager, an uninsulated member or an insulated member. A non-member manager and an uninsulated member shall be deemed to hold the same voting interest as the LLC holds in the next lower tier; a member is uninsulated unless the LLC agreement satisfies the insulation criteria in § 1.5003. An insulated member shall be deemed to hold a voting interest equal to the member's equity interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to LLCs whether they are the licensee, a controlling U.S.-organized parent, or situated above them in the vertical ownership chain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insulation criteria for LP/LLP partners and LLC members
rubrics_metrics.description: A limited partner of a limited partnership and a partner of a limited liability partnership shall be treated as uninsulated unless the partner is prohibited by the operative agreement from, and in fact is not engaged in, active involvement in the management or operation of the partnership and only the usual and customary investor protections are contained in the partnership agreement or other operative agreement. A member of an LLC shall be treated as uninsulated unless the LLC agreement prohibits and the member is not engaged in active management and only usual and customary investor protections are contained in the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These criteria apply to any relevant partnership or LLC anywhere in the vertical ownership chain. For broadcast applicants/licensees, insulation shall be determined in accordance with Note 2(f) of § 73.3555 of this chapter (special broadcast treatment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Usual and customary investor protections (enumerated list)
rubrics_metrics.description: The usual and customary investor protections consist of: (1) the power to prevent sale/pledge of substantially all assets or voluntary bankruptcy/liquidation; (2) the power to prevent entering into contracts with majority investors or their affiliates; (3) the power to prevent guaranteeing obligations of majority investors or their affiliates; (4) the power to purchase additional interest to prevent dilution; (5) the power to prevent change of existing legal rights or preferences as provided in organizational agreements; (6) the power to vote on removal of a general partner/managing member/manager in specified circumstances (bankruptcy, adjudicated incompetence, felony conviction, removal for cause) as determined by an independent party; and (7) the power to prevent amendment of governing agreements with respect to the matters described in (1)-(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission may consider, case-by-case, whether other voting or consent rights constitute usual and customary investor protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate allowance for rulings issued under §1.5000(a)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the foreign ownership interests approved specifically in a licensee's declaratory ruling issued pursuant to §1.5000(a)(1), the controlling U.S.-organized parent named in the ruling may be 100 percent owned, directly and/or indirectly through one or more U.S.- or foreign-organized entities, on a going-forward basis by other foreign investors without prior Commission approval, subject to the requirement that the licensee seek and obtain Commission approval before any foreign individual, entity, or 'group' not previously approved acquires, directly and/or indirectly, more than 5 percent of the U.S. parent's outstanding capital stock and/or voting stock, or a controlling interest, with the exception of any foreign individual, entity, or 'group' that acquires an equity and/or voting interest of 10 percent or less provided that the interest is exempt under § 1.5001(i)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This '100 percent aggregate allowance' lets other foreign investors acquire interests post-ruling but imposes a prior-approval threshold (generally >5%) and references exemptions under §1.5001(i)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate allowance for rulings issued under §1.5000(a)(2) and direct-ownership limit
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the foreign ownership interests approved in a ruling under §1.5000(a)(2), the licensee(s) named may be 100 percent owned in the aggregate by other foreign investors holding interests indirectly through U.S.-organized entities that do not control the licensee, without prior approval, subject to obtaining Commission approval before any previously unapproved foreign investor acquires more than 5 percent of the licensee's equity and/or voting interests (with the same 10 percent exemption under §1.5001(i)(3)). Foreign ownership interests held directly in a licensee shall not be permitted to exceed an aggregate 20 percent of the licensee's equity and/or voting interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes indirect aggregate allowance (subject to 5% prior approval threshold and 10% exemption) from a hard 20% aggregate cap on direct foreign ownership of the licensee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee obligation to monitor foreign ownership and modify organizational documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees have an obligation to monitor and stay ahead of changes in foreign ownership of their controlling U.S.-organized parent companies (for rulings under §1.5000(a)(1)) and/or in the licensee itself (for rulings under §1.5000(a)(2)), to ensure the licensee obtains Commission approval before a change renders it out of compliance with the ruling(s) or the Commission's rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensees, their controlling parent companies, and other entities in the vertical ownership chain may need to place restrictions in their bylaws or other organizational documents to enable compliance with the terms and conditions of declaratory rulings and the Commission's rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage for subsidiaries and affiliates relying on a foreign ownership ruling
rubrics_metrics.description: A foreign ownership ruling issued to a licensee shall cover it and any U.S.-organized subsidiary or affiliate, whether the subsidiary or affiliate existed at the time the ruling was issued or was formed or acquired subsequently, provided that the foreign ownership of the licensee named in the ruling, and of the subsidiary and/or affiliate, remains in compliance with the terms and conditions of the licensee's ruling and the Commission's rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A subsidiary or affiliate may rely on the ruling for filing its own applications provided both it and the licensee certify compliance and include citations of the relevant ruling (DA or FCC Number, FCC Record citation, release date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Insertion of new controlling foreign-organized companies under 100% common ownership/control
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a licensee's foreign ownership ruling specifically authorizes a named foreign investor to hold a controlling interest (in the controlling U.S. parent for §1.5000(a)(1) or in an intervening U.S.-organized entity that does not control the licensee for §1.5000(a)(2)), the ruling shall permit insertion of new, controlling foreign-organized companies in the vertical ownership chain above the controlling U.S. parent or intervening U.S. entity without prior Commission approval provided any new foreign-organized company(ies) are under 100 percent common ownership and control with the foreign investor approved in the ruling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insertion is allowed only when the new foreign-organized company is 100% commonly owned and controlled with the approved foreign investor; separate rules (e.g., section 310(d)) may still require prior approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification for insertion of previously unapproved foreign-organized entities (30-day letter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a previously unapproved foreign-organized entity is inserted into the vertical ownership chain without prior Commission approval pursuant to the 100% common ownership exception, the licensee shall file a letter to the Chief, Office of International Affairs (or Chief, Media Bureau for broadcast) within 30 days after insertion. The letter must include the name of the new entity, a certification that it complies with the 100% common ownership and control requirement, and reference the licensee's foreign ownership ruling(s) by file/citation information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This letter need not be filed if the ownership change is the subject of a pro forma application or notification already filed under applicable service rules. Broadcast stations have special pro forma filing requirements per §73.3540(f) when inserting entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insertion of new non-controlling foreign-organized companies (100% common ownership/control condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a ruling specifically authorizes a named foreign investor to hold a non-controlling interest, the ruling shall permit insertion of new, foreign-organized companies in the vertical ownership chain of the approved foreign investor without prior Commission approval provided any new foreign-organized companies are under 100 percent common ownership and control with the approved foreign investor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors the controlling-insertion rule but applies when the approved interest is non-controlling; specific broadcast and other service rules may add additional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification procedures for insertion of previously unapproved non-controlling foreign-organized entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a previously unapproved foreign-organized entity is inserted pursuant to the non-controlling insertion exception, the licensee shall file a letter to the appropriate FCC office within 30 days including the entity name, a certification of compliance with 100% common ownership/control, and references to the licensee's ruling(s) by file/citation; broadcast licensees must include CDBS File No., Docket No., call sign(s), facility ID(s), and FCC Record citation when available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notification need not be filed if the ownership change is the subject of a pro forma application/notification already filed under the relevant service rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: New petition required before exceeding routine terms and specific conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee that has received a foreign ownership ruling shall file a new petition for declaratory ruling under §1.5000 to obtain Commission approval before its foreign ownership exceeds the routine terms and conditions of this section, and/or any specific terms or conditions of its ruling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to the licensee, U.S.-organized successors-in-interest, and any subsidiary or affiliate relying on the ruling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing compliance — duty to notify Commission of non-compliance within 30 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as specified in paragraph (f)(3), if at any time the licensee (including any successor-in-interest and any subsidiary or affiliate) knows, or has reason to know, that it is no longer in compliance with its foreign ownership ruling or the Commission's rules, it shall file a statement with the Commission explaining the circumstances within 30 days of the date it knew, or had reason to know, that it was no longer in compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent remedial actions do not relieve the licensee of the obligation to notify; the licensee and any controlling companies shall be subject to enforcement actions, including orders requiring divestiture of direct and/or indirect interests.
